title: Yeti Tundra 110 Review
text: This summer I purchased a Yeti Tundra 110 cooler for fishing trips and tailgating, I wanted something that was big, durable, and could keep ice for extended periods of time. While it is probably the most expensive cooler on the market it was worth every penny and so far it has exceed my expectations. I am super impressed by the construction. When I first placed my hands on the Yeti 110 I could tell it was built way better than any other cooler on the market with two inch sidewalls and a solid lid the cooler is virtually indestructible.The Yeti is not made of cheap plastic like other brands. The lid of the cooler has a rubber seal around it, which does an excellent job of locking in the cold air and keeping the warm air out. The non-slip feet on the bottom prevents the cooler from sliding around and damaging other items in the back of my truck like fishing rods and groceries. The T-rex latches are sturdy and durable unlike the cheap plastic latches that are constantly breaking on other coolers.The cooler is definitely heavier than most, but the rope handles makes it very easy for two people to carry from one place to another. There are two drain plugs on the side that allow for easy water drainage.The first time I used the cooler was on a fishing trip. We packed the cooler with food and drinks, and during the 10-hour trip, we had very little ice melt despite sitting out in the sun all dayThe 110 is a perfect size when hosting tailgates. This single cooler does the work of two, and can hold over 80 cans along with 40 pounds of ice. Its large size allows me to hold beverages for everyone in our tailgate. Even after being opened and closed all day long it did a great job of keeping ice.Another great reason to buy this cooler it all the cool accessories that can be added, such as a seat cushion, drain hose and bear-proof locks.  Although the first accessory I would recommend is the security cable lock and bracket to keep it safely stored in the back of your truck.  This cooler is perfect for a person looking for a high quality durable cooler that can stand up to the abuse of being used time and time again, while keeping all your food and beverages cold for extended periods of time.

title: I was skeptical, but needed a quality cooler.  Shasta Lake for 10 days last summer.
text: I did not want to pay this much for a cooler.  I did my research and discovered that some of the other brands *MAY* be better.  BUT, I found the "TESTS" I watched online to be inconsistent.  In the end, the fact that Yeti is established, you can get parts, there is a warranty, and it will retain some value should I wish to sell it, convinced me that Yeti was the right choice.So I plunked down the dough and a few days later it showed up on my porch. Box was beat, but contents in fine shape. Ours is white and came with the food basket in it, but no divider.  I happened to have part of a left-over sheet of black 1/4" HDPE (marine wood) so I made one.Before the 10 day trip to Lake Shasta we decided to use the Yeti for meat.  So we froze all the steaks, burgers, chicken, bacon, and sausage.  I also froze 4 half gallon old orange juice bottles filled with water.  We filled the Yeti with frozen meat and bottles of water and headed to Shasta.First, let me say that this 105 is a big deep ice chest.  I needed it to be pretty big, and I wanted it to be deep rather than wide.  This is personal preference, a deep chest takes up less floor space than a wide shallow chest, but it also means that finding items in the bottom can be challenging.  However, if the chest is very wide it become difficult to carry and get through doors.At the lake it was between 93 and 105 degrees and 70-80 at night.  Never the less, the Yeti kept the meat completely frozen for 6 days.  As we took meat out each day we tried to keep the lid shut of course.  As meat was removed the frozen bottles of water began to thaw but the meat stayed substantially frozen.  We added some ice at day 6, but even though the house boat had two propane powered refrigerator/freezers, we never felt we needed to move the meat to the refrigerators.On day 8 we added a little ice, and by day 10 we still had 3 pounds of very very cold bacon to take back home.I also have an Igloo Marine 110 with wheels which we use for keeping drinks cold.  Because people are in and out of it all the time we use a LOT of ice.  Between the small carry chests and the big Igoo we go through 20+ pounds per day, but the Yeti kept all our meat cool with very little ice.  I was very impressed.I don't know if an ice chest this expensive will be necessary for weekend trips, but it sure worked well for out long trip.

title: Wow! All the hype on the Yeti actually lives up to reality.
text: I'm one of those people that reads all the reviews, questions and answers. I went all over the web and watched almost every YouTube review on the Yeti. Let's face it if you're going to fork over $500 for a cooler you want to make sure it's exceptional, I don't care how much money you have. The Yeti 110 lives up to the hype. I'm not saying that because I want to justify dropping 5 Franklins for an ice chest. After many years of one week camping trips into the woods only to have the ice disappear after 2-3 days, I wanted something that works. We headed off to the woods into the San Bernadeno National Forest last week. Even at 7,000 ft the daytime temps reached into the mid-eighties (August). When we got home on day 7 and there was plenty of still ice in the chest keeping things cool. Amazing actually, and I don't amaze easily anymore. Tips: 1) Pre-cool the chest the day before departure and add your working ice the day of departure. 2) Block ice on the bottom helps, or as we did, freeze up four 1 gallon water bottles (you now have extra drinking water also), then add your bags of ice. 3) Keep the cooler in the shade (duh). 4) Wet down a large towel and place it over the chest, the evaporation will keep the top cool, re-wet towel as it dries. 5) Pre-cool all your drinks before adding them to the chest. 6) Keep your chest off the ground. 7) Get in and out quickly, air is the enemy. 8) and here's a secret weapon against melting for all coolers: I cut a piece of sheet foam insulation (styro-foam packing sheets work great) to fit and place it inside the chest over the ice. Yes, the Yeti is very spendy, but it is well built, will last years, and it works. BTW, didn't encounter any bears this trip, so I can't speak to the "Bear Proof" rating.

title: Heavy-Duty and Spacious Cooler
text: The YETI Tundra 110 is a large, sturdy cooler with plenty of room for food and drinks. It feels extremely well built and is great for boating, camping, fishing, or large outdoor gatherings. The heavy-duty construction gives it a durable feel, and the size is perfect when you need to pack a lot. Overall, an excellent cooler for outdoor use.

title: Yeti Tunda 105 Cooler
text: We’re very happy with our cooler! It kept all of our food cold and frozen just as promised, and it worked great for our needs. The only downside is that it’s pretty heavy, especially when it’s loaded with food. I do wish it had wheels to make it easier to move around. Overall, though, we’re very happy with our purchase!

title: Keeps ice cold for a social event, hard to move when loaded up.
text: Kept drinks really cold at a work picnic from 11 - 4 no problem.  I put a large Yeti ice on the bottom, and alternated layers of ice and prechilled drinks and it worked great.  Drinks ended up colder than typical fridge temp.  Fully loaded, it's a pain to move and definitely needs 2 people.  Considering getting some sort of wheeled solution to help w/ moving it if it needs to be mobile.  A work proximity associate's cute dog gnawed on the cooler a bit, but it held up with no marks.Not the best value for money as a typical cooler can probably do the same thing, but I like it.
